# Implementation

> Last verified against the code: 2026-11-20 (commit 68010d3 + the Framer home page)

How each part is built, file by file.

## Pages (all generated by `scripts/build_work.py`)

- **Home** (`index.html`): the first card is Taylor (`ME`: the green portrait, opens About), then the projects. One screen that scales with the window like the reference, measured at 1024 × 768, 1280 × 1000, 1440 × 900 and 2000 × 1220. Text sits at 40 px in a centred 1520 px column (28 px serif title and type). The card (`--card`) is 299 px from 810 to 1199 px wide and `13.1vw + 197px` (capped at 48vh) from 1200 px up, with a 4 px white border and a 0 10px 25px shadow, centred at 55% / 52.9% of the height (`--cy`). Side cards sit .914 / 1.552 / 2.104 card-widths out and drop .207 / .396 / .526, at scale .669 / .495 / .495 and 6 / 12 / 16°; the arrows (24 px) sit .689 card below centre; the menu is 56 px from the bottom. Between the arrows and the menu, `.home-logos` runs the `LOGOS` list as an endless row (two copies, CSS `translateX(-50%)` over 48 s, faded at the edges; still for reduced motion, hidden on desktop windows under 760 px tall). The stage clips the outer cards. `assets/carousel.js` places each card by its distance from the centre (offset, drop, scale 1 / .665 / .49 / .475, tilt 0 / 6 / 12 / 16°, measured on the reference), moves on the arrows, arrow keys, swipes, the mouse wheel or trackpad (one project per gesture: deltas add up past a threshold, then the rest of the gesture is ignored until it pauses for 180 ms) and clicks on side cards, and lets the centre card open its case study. Cards fan out from the centre on load. Every card is greyscale until it is the centre card (`.is-center`). A project with a `hero_clip` also gets a `.slide-video` in its card: `carousel.js` sets its source only when that card is centred, plays it muted and looping, fades it in once it is playing and pauses it when the card leaves (or the tab is hidden); nothing plays for reduced motion. Work and More-to-explore cards turn colour on hover. Transform and opacity only.
- **Work** (`work/index.html`): "Selected work", then all projects in two columns (`.w-card`; right-column cards square, left 4:3), name in serif, type and year.
- **About** (`about/index.html`), matched to the reference's About: the statement (each word a `<span>`; `assets/about.js` darkens them in sequence once when it comes into view), two paragraphs and two photos in a 38/24/33 split; a black band (`.dark`) with the experience rows (`.job`: + marker, title and description, company, years) and the five services as a deck (`.deck-slide`, each listing its projects from `ABOUT["service_work"]`): from 810 px one framed 16:9 slide shows at a time in a pinned band with a segmented progress bar, counter and arrows, and `about.js` steps through them as the page scrolls (the band is one 90%-screen step per slide; arrows and segments scroll to a slide; hidden slides are `inert`); on phones the slides stack; **In numbers.**; the logo strip. No testimonials until real ones are supplied. From 1200 px up it follows the reference at 1440 × 900: a 64 px statement, the photos placed absolutely (small at 41.5% / big flush right, overlapping the statement's last line), experience on the light page with a 48 px serif heading, and the services as a deck (see below).
- **Case studies** (`work/<slug>/index.html`): see `assets/main.css` below.

Every page shares the menu (`nav()`: Home, About, Work, Contact) and the black footer (`FOOT`). The home page carries the schema.org `Person` search profile (`application/ld+json`).

## `404.html` (page not found)

GitHub Pages serves it for any missing address, so every path in it is root-absolute. It uses `assets/main.css` (the `.not-found` block), has `noindex`, and links home and to the work.

## `scripts/build_work.py`

`PROJECTS` is a list of dicts with these keys:

- `slug`, `client`, `title`, `year`, `role`, `disciplines`
- `hero_img`, and optionally `hero_clip` (a local loop), `hero_vimeo` (an HD Vimeo background) and `hero_light` (a white render, which gets a dark title band)
- `lead`, `body` (paragraphs) and `figures` (number, label)
- optionally `film` (`yt`, `vimeo` or `video`, plus `title`), `link` (label, URL) and `gallery` (shown only with two or more images)

`PROJECTS` holds the fourteen projects in carousel order (slugs: `superfile-trackhouse-nascar`, `superfile-brand-launch`, `wylie-co`, `flex-lafc`, `superfile-ufc-wwe`, `superfile-lefty-out-there`, `superfile-lafc`, `superfile-trackhouse-motogp`, `ego`, `skil`, `superfile-art-car`, `flex-launch`, `digital-domain`, `ego-labs`). Each has `name` and `type` (as on the cards), `card` (the card image; the case-page hero defaults to its `@2x`), and the case-study fields. Each case study also has `role_text` (paragraphs for "Taylor's role.") and `sections` (a heading, paragraphs and optional `img`: one image full width, two or more in pairs). `page(p, more)` renders a case study (see `assets/main.css` below); `more` is the next two projects in `PROJECTS`, wrapping from the last to the first. Gallery photos that repeat the hero are skipped. It also sets per-page `<title>`, description and Open Graph tags. Pages use root-absolute paths (`/assets/...`), so they work only from the site root, which is how Pages and the local preview serve them.

`V` sets the `?v=` cache stamp on `main.css`, `carousel.js` and `site.js` on every generated page; keep `404.html` equal.

## Card images

Card originals live ungraded in `sources/cards/<name>.jpg`. `scripts/grade_cards.sh` writes `assets/home/work/<name>@2x.jpg` (up to 2048 px) and `<name>.jpg` (1024 px) with one cinematic grade: contrast 1.14, saturation .86, cool shadows and warm highlights, a vignette and light grain. The portrait card (`taylor-powers`) is not graded. To change a card, replace its original and re-run the script.

## `assets/site.js`

Used by the case pages (it was also the old home page's script; the Intro, Reel, Clips and Clock parts now find no elements and do nothing). The script is one IIFE, and every part guards for missing elements.

| Part | Details |
|---|---|
| Intro | Removes `#intro` after 1.3 s, or at once if seen this session or under reduced motion |
| Visibility | One IntersectionObserver pauses any video off screen. Videos marked `data-auto` (the reel, case heroes) resume when visible |
| Reel | Sound toggle, progress line, and the header's `.solid` state |
| HD heroes | Listens for Vimeo `play`, `playProgress` and `timeupdate` messages from `.case-hero-vimeo`. On the first one it fades the iframe in (`.on`) and pauses the local clip. Under reduced motion the iframe is removed |
| Clips | `startClip` and `stopClip` set `src` from `data-src` on first use and toggle `.playing`. Hover drives them on desktop; a centered-on-screen observer (`rootMargin -35%`) drives them on touch |
| Fade-ins | `.tile` elements fade up once (`html.js`, `.in`) |
| Clock | `Intl.DateTimeFormat` for America/Chicago, refreshed every 15 s |
| Lightbox | Builds a `<video>` or `<iframe>` and pauses every other video. On close it clears the frame and resumes visible `data-auto` videos |

## `assets/main.css` (case studies, and every other page)

Laid out like a Framer portfolio template the owner chose (2026-11-20) and asked to match exactly: grey page (`--bg #f4f4f4`), square-cornered images, Baskervville serif (Google Fonts) for headings, navigation and figures, Switzer for text (the template's BDO Grotesk isn't on Google Fonts; Switzer is the close match already self-hosted). Two `1fr` columns with a 16 px gap inside 40 px margins (20 px on phones). In page order:

1. **Navigation** (`.nav`, over the hero): **Home** and **Work** centred, **Contact ↗** on the right.
2. **Hero** (`.hero`, full screen): the image, local clip or Vimeo background (`.case-hero-vimeo`), easing in from 108% scale on load, under a dark gradient. **← All Works** bottom left; in the right column the title (56 px serif), the lead and a facts table (`.facts`: Client, Year, Type = the first discipline). `hero_light` renders (`.light-hero`) sit contained on the grey with dark text.
3. **Intro band** (`.intro`, black): the body paragraphs at 20/24 px in the right column.
4. **Taylor's role.** (`.row`): serif heading left; the role and the disciplines in grey on the right.
5. **Media** (`.media`): the film as a full-width 3:2 still (`.full.film`) with **Watch the film**; photos (skipping any that repeat the hero) in square pairs (`.pair`), or one full width.
6. **Results.** / **Coverage.** (`.row`): the figures (44 px serif) and the coverage link.
7. **More to explore.** (`.more`): the next two projects, images at 449:334, serif names.
8. **Footer** (`.foot`, black): "Let's" plus a rotating phrase (work together. / connect. / create., a CSS animation, off under reduced motion), "Based in Chicago", LinkedIn and All work links, the email pill, and the copyright line.

Below 810 px everything stacks into one column. The same file also styles `404.html` (`.case-bar`, `.not-found`, `.case-foot`) and the lightbox (`.player`).

`assets/site.css` (the old dark Archivo styles) was removed on 2026-11-20.

## Media

| Folder | Contents | How it was made |
|---|---|---|
| `assets/video/` | `reel.mp4` (1080p H.264, 45 s, about 5.6 MB) and `reel-poster.jpg` | The owner's showreel, re-saved with the index at the front (fast start) |
| `assets/clips/` | `ego`, `flex-falcon`, `flex-soccer`, `skil` (`.mp4` and `.jpg`) | Cut silent from the reel (EGO 4.4–7.9 s, falcon 19.4–22.6 s, soccer 30.0–34.6 s, SKIL 26.9–30.2 s), 1280×720 H.264 at about 2.2 Mbps, about 1 MB each |
| `assets/img/` | `daytona-race`, `ufc-wwe`, `motogp-superfile`, `art-car`, `vm-1014838410`, `flex-lafc-welcome`, `taylor-portrait` | See [CONTENT.md](CONTENT.md) for the source of each |
| `assets/logos/` | 13 SVGs | Wikimedia Commons, Simple Icons and the brands' own sites |

## Gaps

- No HD footage yet for EGO, SKIL, MotoGP, UFC & WWE or Daytona.
- The portrait is 800×800.
- GitHub Pages can't set response headers: the CSP and referrer policy are `<meta>` tags in every page (the case pages get them from the template in `scripts/build_work.py`); HSTS and anti-framing headers aren't possible there, and the domain has no DMARC or CAA records yet. See [OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md).
